business: The Aldera: magnesium in single-serve capsule sachets (pure bisglycinate and a 3-form complex)
by_segment: Prime replenisher who reorders the same bottle
by_behaviour: Travels and packs pills in a pill case
why_not: NONE. The first thing I noticed was $29.99 for 30 servings, which is a dollar a day when Nature Made or Double Wood run 20 to 40 cents, and then zero reviews. I spend 20 minutes on reviews before I try anything new and there is nothing here to read.

NONE. The first thing I noticed was the sachets, which is actually what I want for travel, but then the $29.99 and zero reviews. That is $1 a serving when Nature Made or Double Wood are $0.20-0.40, and I do not buy supplements with no reviews, I read the 1-star ones first.

NONE. First thing I noticed was '200 mg' on the front, and then that it is two capsules, which is fine, but $29.99 for 30 days is $1.00 a day when I know Nature Made is about $0.39. The sachets suit my flying and the lab QR is a nice touch, but a brand with zero reviews does not get 2.5x the price from me.

NONE. First thing I noticed was $29.99 for 30 sachets, which is about $1.00 a day, and my Nature Made 200 mg is around $0.39 a day. I already have a magnesium that works for me, and a new brand with zero reviews doesn't give me a reason to pay almost 3x.

NONE. The first thing I noticed was the 2 capsules in every sachet, and nothing tells me how big they are, so I would have to read reviews first and there are none. I already reorder a magnesium that works for me, and $29.99 for 30 days is about $1 a day, which is more than I pay now.

NONE. The first thing I noticed was $29.99 for 30 sachets, which is about $1.00 a day, and my Nature Made is about $0.39 a day and already works for me. The QR lab report is nice, but I'm not paying more than double for a brand with no reviews.

NONE. The first thing I noticed was 200 mg per sachet in 2 capsules, and bisglycinate at that dose usually means big size 00 capsules, which I can't swallow comfortably. The lab-tested QR is a nice touch, but with no reviews and no capsule size listed I'm not risking $30 on a box I may not be able to take.

NONE. First thing I noticed is 2 capsules in every sachet and 200 mg per serving, and nowhere does it say how big the capsules are. I have left bad reviews on huge capsules, and a new brand with zero reviews is not getting my money to find out.

NONE. The first thing I noticed was the "Every batch lab-tested" line with the QR code, which I like, but then I saw 30 individual foil sachets with 2 capsules each and thought that is a lot of trash for something I take at home at night. At $1 a day with no reviews and no NSF or USP seal, I would stay with my bottle.

NONE. The first thing I noticed was 30 foil sachets in a box, and my reaction was that it's a lot of packaging for 60 capsules I'd just dump into my weekly organizer anyway. The QR lab report is nice, but I'd rather pay for the magnesium than the wrapper.
why_yes: PURE. First thing I noticed was 'no magnesium oxide' and the 'Every batch lab-tested' line with the QR, plus sachets I can toss in a carry-on since I fly every few weeks. I'd try one box of the bisglycinate only, and only move it to Subscribe & Save if it doesn't bother my stomach.

PURE. The first thing I checked was whether 200 mg was really two capsules, and the box says it plainly (100 mg per capsule, 2 in each sachet), so no trick there. What I noticed next was the 'Every batch lab-tested' line with the QR code, and I would scan it before ordering. For sleep I want bisglycinate with no oxide, and $1 a serving is fair for that.

PURE. The first thing I noticed was "200 mg" on the front, and then I saw it is two capsules of 100 mg each, so I did the math: $1.00 a day against about $0.39 for Nature Made. But it is real bisglycinate with no oxide, the sachets fit in my carry-on, and the QR batch report is something I can actually check, so I would try one box for travel and sleep.

PURE. The first thing I noticed was the sachets: one a day, pocket-sized, tear open with one hand, which is exactly what I need in a carry-on every few weeks. The 200 mg is clearly 2 capsules of 100 mg and the QR batch report helps, so I would try one box, but not on auto-ship until I see it works.

PURE. What I noticed first was the QR code and 'Every batch lab-tested' on the front, plus that it's plain bisglycinate with no citrate, which is what gives me cramps. I'd try one box to see if it's gentle on my stomach, but only one, since there are no reviews yet.

PURE. The first thing I noticed was 'no magnesium oxide' and the QR on every sachet, plus the sachets fit my travel pill case. The complex has citrate in it, which gives me cramps, so I skip that one and try one box of the bisglycinate.
